findings.finding: The new schema field `antipattern_id` references a value vocabulary that is never fully defined. code-review-tests.md names its antipatterns by bolded prose headings ('fail-open oracle', 'unrealistic fault injection', 'contract-contradicting assertion') and its guards by parenthesized numbers (i)-(x), not by canonical machine ids, so what literal token an executor writes is implicit. More critically, the three #12-native 'additional instances' (a fixture mutating state it did not create; an equivalence test using different hardening helpers; a policy-preference oracle) are, by the plan's own words, 'verified absent from the rubric' — so their antipattern_id must be a 'portable-core id', but the plan never establishes that the portable core in references/patterns.md defines named ids for those three classes.
findings.location: Approach > Evidence shape (`antipattern_id` field); Approach > Additional instances; references/patterns.md portable core
scenarios: A discovery subagent files a #12 finding for a fixture that mutates state it did not create and must populate antipattern_id, but no id token exists for that class in either the rubric or the (as-specified) portable core
